subject: ACME PDM - streaming token duplication observed when SDK prefetch + dedicated routing
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: ACME PDM - streaming token duplication observed when SDK prefetch + dedicated routing

Team —

ACME (prod-team@acme.com) reported a production issue this morning: their streaming clients intermittently receive duplicated token chunks that break their JSON streaming consumer (they see repeated tokens like "}}" and partial JSON objects). They reproduce reliably when using our Java SDK with prefetch enabled against their Dedicated pool (pool-id: acme-dedicated-1).

What I have so far:
- Customer environment: dedicated pool pinned to rtxX-large in us-west-2; SDK v1.12.0 with PREFETCH=enabled; using streaming with function-calls enabled.
- Repro: attached acme_prefetch_repro.har contains the single-session traffic and acme_streaming_sample.log has the raw responses.
- Impact: customer called this P1 for their ingestion pipeline (they buffer streamed JSON objects).

Ask: can Platform/Runtime triage whether prefetch + dedicated routing could cause duplicate token emission? Quick ask items: 
1) Is there a known interaction between our prefetch path and routing/fallback that might double-apply KV-cache/prefixes?
2) If not, can we reproduce and confirm root cause within 48h?
3) Short-term mitigation: can we disable prefetch at the pool level for ACME or route them to hosted fallback while we patch?

Please see attached repro and logs. I know this overlaps with an area where Karthik has prior work; tagging you for visibility. Dev — if you can try the HAR locally and share repro steps that’d help. Marissa — customer is nervous and asking for an ETA; they may ask for credit if we can’t get them back to stable quickly.

Thanks —
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

Attachment stubs: acme_prefetch_repro.har (network capture), acme_streaming_sample.log (raw server responses)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME PDM - streaming token duplication observed when SDK prefetch + dedicated routing

Thanks for the reproduction and logs, Soojin. Hypothesis off the bat: the prefetch path applies a prefix/KV set into the runtime cache on the client side, and if a request is re-routed (for capacity/failover) we may be re-applying the same prefix on the server leading to duplicated emission when streaming resumes. I don’t think we’ve seen this exact symptom before, but it’s plausible given some recent routing changes that introduced a short-lived transient reconnection path.

Immediate plan:
- Dev — can you run the HAR locally against a dev runtime with prefetch on and see if you can trigger duplication? If yes, capture sequence numbers (X-Seq) and token boundaries.
- I’ll open a Jira (INF-4521) and propose a canary patch that adds an idempotency check to prefix application (fast guard): if prefix-id already present in session, skip re-apply. This should be low-risk and patchable without model changes.
- If we can’t confirm quickly, my suggested short-term mitigation is disabling PREFETCH at the pool level for acme-dedicated-1. That’s a configuration flip and should be reversible.

Timeline ask: repro attempt today; patch + canary tomorrow night UTC if repro confirmed.

Marissa — if we do a pool-level flip, we should communicate the customer impact and whether they prefer fallback to hosted vs. disabling prefetch.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal PM, Runtime

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 13:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME PDM - streaming token duplication observed when SDK prefetch + dedicated routing

I pulled the HAR and replayed the session against a dev runtime (branch: feature/prefetch-idempotency-test). Repro is consistent when prefetch is enabled and the client reconnects within ~300ms (we added an artificial route-fail to force a reconnect). Observations:
- Sequence header behavior: when reconnect happens, the runtime applied the cached prefix twice (see log lines with seq 112/113). The second apply emits the same token boundary causing clients that concatenate chunks to get duplicate fragments.
- Quick repro command (local):
  1) docker run --rm -e PREFETCH=1 -p 8080:8080 runtime-dev:latest
  2) python replay_har.py acme_prefetch_repro.har --endpoint http://localhost:8080 --inject-route-fail 300

Logs attached: acme_streaming_sample.log (trimmed).

Short-term mitigations I can implement today: 
A) Add a server-side guard: check session.prefetch_applied_ids and skip duplicate prefix application. I can push a hotfix to canary in ~6-8 hours if no regressions.
B) If Marissa/Customer prefers immediate operational fix, we can flip PREFETCH=false for acme-dedicated-1 via our config service. That will stop prefetch traffic immediately.

I’ll start INF-4521 and add my repro steps + patch diff.

—Dev
Dev Patel
SRE/Runtime Engineer

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME PDM - streaming token duplication observed when SDK prefetch + dedicated routing

Thanks for the fast triage. Quick customer context: ACME is mid-deal expansion (add-on ingestion pipeline) with committed spend starting next month; they are sensitive to downtime or data loss. They’ve asked specifically: do you need us to move traffic to hosted fallback or will the PREFETCH flip be transparent?

From a commercial perspective: if we must route them to hosted for stability for an extended window, we should prepare a short-term credit offer and coordinate ramp-back messaging. If it’s a single-night patch on the runtime canary and we can disable PREFETCH while that lands, they are ok with that as long as we share a clear timeline.

Customer asks from their side (quoted):
> "We can tolerate a short window where data is buffered on our side, but we need assurance the duplicates won't corrupt the stream. Please keep us posted on the exact UTC window for the fix."

Soojin — please confirm whether they prefer PREFETCH disable vs hosted fallback. Also open to pinging support to prepare a post-mortem template.

—Marissa

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 24 Apr 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: ACME PDM - streaming corruption examples (customer)

Forwarding customer note and confirmation.

---------- Forwarded message ---------
From: Claire Barnes <claire@acme-pdm.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 at 07:58:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Streaming issues this morning
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Thanks for the quick help. We saw the duplicated tokens starting ~07:30 PDT and it impacted ~2% of our streams. We've attached a sample from our consumer logs showing the duplicated fragments. For now we can accept PREFETCH being turned off for our dedicated pool if that prevents the issue. Please advise on timing for the fix.

—Claire
Product Ops, ACME PDM
claire@acme-pdm.com

---------- End forwarded message ---------

Update / agreed actions: 
- INF-4521 created (JIRA). Owner: dev_patel.
- Short-term: Operations will flip PREFETCH=false for acme-dedicated-1 at 2027-04-25T02:00:00Z (scheduled 30-min maintenance window). Ops on-call will monitor.
- Medium-term: Dev will land idempotency guard into runtime canary and run regression tests (target canary on 2027-04-25 UTC window + roll to prod after validation).
- Communication: Marissa to send a customer note with the scheduled window and offer a small credit if they see any residual impact.

Attachments: acme_prefetch_repro.har, acme_streaming_sample.log, acme_prefetch_toggle_screenshot.png

Thanks all — I will update the customer thread and HubSpot.

Soojin
